SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r4.claim: The words ‘We enjoined’ are God’s speech, an interjection in Luqman’s testament before his counsel resumes, rather than Luqman speaking.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r4.anchor: هذه ليست وصية لقمان، هذا كلام الله، لقمان لم ينه وصيته، هذه مداخلة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r5.claim: God takes over the injunction to honor parents because their standing before Him is so great.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r5.anchor: فلما كان شأن الوالدين عظيما تولى ربنا تعالى أمرهما، لعظم منزلتهما عند الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r1.claim: The command to honor parents interrupts Luqman's advice and reinforces its prohibition of shirk.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r1.anchor: اعتراض في أثناء وصية لقمان تأكيدا لما فيها من النهي عن الشرك

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r2.claim: The passage highlights the mother's right and the parents' great claim: she carried the child through weakness upon weakness, then nursed until weaning.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r2.anchor: ثم رجح الأم ونبه على عظم حق والديه

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r3.claim: Wahn is weakness in constitution and character; as the fetus grows, the mother's weakness increases until delivery.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r3.anchor: والوهن الضعف من حيث الخلق والخلق

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r4.claim: Fisal is separation from nursing, as a camel calf is called fasīl when weaned from its mother.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r4.anchor: الفصال التفريق بين الصبي والرضاع ومنه الفصيل

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r5.claim: The text distinguishes عام as often associated with ease from سنة, often used for hardship or drought; weaning is completed at two years from birth.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r5.anchor: لكن كثيرا ما تستعمل السنة في الحول الذي فيه الشدة والجدب

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r6.claim: For al-Shafii, suckling through two years establishes milk kinship; it is obligatory until the child is self-sufficient, recommended through two years, and permissible through two and a half, while the disagreement concerns milk kinship.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r6.anchor: وهي مدة الرضاع عند الشافعي فلا يثبت حرمة الرضاع

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r7.claim: By agreement, the father's nursing-wage obligation is limited to two years and does not continue afterward.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r7.anchor: أما استحقاق الأجرة فمقدر بحولين فلا تجب نفقة الإرضاع

BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r8.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r8.claim: The verse recalls the mother's hardship in nursing the child for two years after birth.
BURSEVI:v7p58#3/r8.anchor: قال في الوسيط : المعنى ذكر مشقة الوالدة

BURSEVI:v7p59/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r1.claim: An ushkur li either explains the command to thank God or gives its purpose; the intervening words particularly reinforce the duty to the mother.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r1.anchor: تفسير لوصيناه أي : قلنا له اشكر لي

BURSEVI:v7p59/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r2.claim: When asked whom to honor most, the Prophet answered “your mother” three times, then “your father.”
BURSEVI:v7p59/r2.anchor: لمن قال له من أبر "أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك"

BURSEVI:v7p59/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r3.claim: Thank God for creating and guiding you to Islam, and thank parents for raising you; gratitude to God is reverence and glorification, while gratitude to parents is compassion and respect.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r3.anchor: اشكر لي حيث أوجدتك وهديتك بالإسلام واشكر لوالديك حيث ربيّاك صغيرا

BURSEVI:v7p59/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r4.claim: Sharh al-Hikam says their gratitude is joined to God's because parents are the proximate, figurative cause of existence, while God is its true source.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r4.anchor: قرن شكرهما بشكره إذ هما أصل وجودك المجازي

BURSEVI:v7p59/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r5.claim: The hadith that one who does not thank people does not thank God means either that thanking people is a condition for valid gratitude to God or that God's reward goes only to those who thank His servants.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث "لا يشكر الله من لا يشكر الناس" فجعل شكر الناس

BURSEVI:v7p59/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59/r6.claim: A teacher's right to gratitude exceeds a parent's; Alexander says his father brought him down from heaven to earth while his tutor raised him from earth to heaven.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r6.anchor: ثم حق المعلم في الشكر فوق حق الوالدين

BURSEVI:v7p59/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59/r7.speaker: برزجمهر
BURSEVI:v7p59/r7.claim: He says he honors his teacher more because his father caused his mortal life, while his teacher caused his lasting life.
BURSEVI:v7p59/r7.anchor: لبرزجمهر ما بالك تعظيمك لمعلمك أشد

BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r1.claim: The return to God explains why obedience is required: people return to Him alone and He will reward gratitude or ingratitude.
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r1.anchor: تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بالأمر أي : إلى الرجوع

BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r2.claim: Returning to God means reaching a state where no judge or owner exists but Him.
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r2.anchor: الرجوع إلى الله الرجوع إلى حيث لا حاكم ولا مالك سواه

BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r3.claim: He says the five daily prayers thank God, while praying for one's parents after those prayers thanks them.
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r3.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة : من صلى الصلوات الخمس

BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r4.claim: A report says that honoring a deceased father includes maintaining ties with his friends; if parents died while one was undutiful, prayer and charity for them afterward can restore filial piety.
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أحب أن يصل أباه في قبره

BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r5.claim: A report from al-Ihya and Qut al-Qulub prescribes two Thursday-night rakahs with specified repeated recitations, followed by fifteen istighfars dedicated to parents; it says this fulfills their right even for a disobedient child.
BURSEVI:v7p59#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من صلى ليلة الخميس ما بين المغرب والعشاء ركعتين

SULAMI:v2p130#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p130#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p130#3/r1.claim: Thank God for creating you and thank your parents as the cause of your existence; absorption in gratitude to the ultimate Cause may eclipse gratitude to the means, while failure to realize the Cause returns one to thanking the means.
SULAMI:v2p130#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء - رحمة الله عليه - اشكره حيث اوجدك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r1.claim: وهنا على وهن means weakness upon weakness.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r1.anchor: على وهن} أي ضعفا على ضعف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p344#3/r2.anchor: وهنا على وهن} أي ضعفا على ضعف. {وفصاله} فطامه

NAHHAS:v3p285/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p285/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p285/r2.claim: The instruction to honor parents interrupts Luqman’s speech to his son.

NAHHAS:v3p285/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p285/r3.speaker: سعد
NAHHAS:v3p285/r3.claim: Saʿd reports that his mother swore not to eat or drink until he renounced Muhammad; relatives fed her by prying her mouth open, and the verse about parents was revealed.
NAHHAS:v3p285/r3.anchor: كما روى شعبة عن سماك بن حرب عن مصعب بن سعد عن أبيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r1.claim: Gratitude benefits the grateful person, not God: its fruits perfect the worshipper, while God needs no thanks; the conditional and exclusive wording stresses this relation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r1.anchor: وللتنبيه على هذا المعنى أعقب الله الشكر المأمور به ببيان أن فائدته لنفس الشاكر لا للمشكور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r2.claim: Turning from gratitude is ingratitude for a blessing, but God is self-sufficient and praiseworthy; human benefactors may gain reciprocal benefits from gratitude, unlike God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r2.anchor: لإفادة أن الإعراض عن الشكر بعد استشعاره كفر للنعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r3.claim: God is praised by all creation, even the unbeliever's condition, as 13:15 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r3.anchor: كثير المحمودية بلسان حال الكائنات كلها حتى حال الكافر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r4.claim: أن اشكر لله condenses Luqman's core wisdom and begins the requested gratitude immediately upon receiving a blessing; الحمد رأس الشكر is cited, and حميد is used because God has no name from the gratitude root except الشكور.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r4.anchor: جامعا لمبدأ الحكمة التي أوتيها لقمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r5.claim: The present tense in يشكر signals renewed gratitude, and the لام in اشكر لي is a strengthening marker conventionally attached to the verb شكر, as in 2:152.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p152/r5.anchor: لام ملتزم زيادتها مع مادة الشكر للتأكيد والتقوية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r2.claim: The instruction gives mother and father equal standing, then singles out the mother for pregnancy and nursing, yielding three shares of kindness for her and one for the father; the Prophetic answer names the mother three times, then the father.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r2.anchor: ثم خصص الأم بدرجة ذكر الحمل ودرجة ذكر الرضاع فتحصل للأم ثلاث مراتب وللأب واحدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r3.claim: Wahnan ʿalā wahn can mean weakness upon weakness from pregnancy then childbirth, the weakness of child and mother, or steadily increasing weakness without specifying two episodes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r3.anchor: وهنا على وهن معناه ضعفا على ضعف، وقيل إشارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r4.speaker: عيسى الثقفي وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r4.claim: They read wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ; it has the same meaning as the majority reading with sukūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي «وهنا على وهن» بفتح الهاء، ورويت عن أبي عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء والجحدري ويعقوب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r5.claim: They read wa-faṣluhu instead of wa-fiṣāluhu; the author says fiṣāl points to the counted duration of nursing by naming its endpoint.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «وفصاله» ، وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r6.claim: Jurists agree on two years as the nursing period for maintenance, but differ on milk kinship: exactly two years, two years plus connected days, or no effect after early weaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r6.anchor: والناس مجمعون على العامين في مدة الرضاع في باب الأحكام والنفقات، وأما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r7.claim: Sufyan says praying the five daily prayers thanks God, while praying for one's parents after them thanks one's parents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r7.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r8.claim: The clause ilaa al-maṣīr inserts a warning within the parental counsel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إلي المصير توعد أثناء الوصية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r1.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ; the author refers readers to his account in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت في سعد بن أبي وقاص وقد شرحنا ذلك في العنكبوت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r2.speaker: الضحاك وعاصم الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read “wahn” with fatḥa on the hāʾ both times; al-Zajjāj glosses it as weakness upon weakness from successive burdens of pregnancy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r2.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك وعاصم الجحدري وهنا على وهن بفتح الهاء فيهما قال الزجاج أي ضعفا على ضعف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r3.claim: The accusative “an” introduces the command enjoining gratitude to God and to one’s parents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r3.anchor: وموضع أن نصب ب وصينا المعنى ووصينا الإنسان أن أشكر لي ولواليدك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r4.claim: “Its weaning is in two years” means weaning occurs at the completion of two years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r4.anchor: أي فطامه يقع في انقضاء عامين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي وأبو عمران والأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿImrān, and al-Aʿmash read “fiṣālihi” with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r5.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي وأبو عمران والأعمش وفصاله بفتح الفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب والحسن وأبو رجاء وطلحة بن مصرف وعاصم الجحدري وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r6.claim: These authorities read “faṣlihi” with fatḥa on fāʾ, sukūn on ṣād, and no alif; the wording highlights the mother’s hardship in nursing after pregnancy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p319/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب والحسن وأبو رجاء وطلحة بن مصرف وعاصم الجحدري وقتادة وفصله بفتح الفاء وسكون الصاد من غير ألف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.claim: Worship of God alone is paired with kindness to parents, as in 17:23 and often elsewhere in the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.anchor: وكثيرا ما يقرن تعالى بين ذلك في القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r4.claim: Mujāhid interprets the mother's weakness upon weakness as the hardship of carrying her child; Qatādah says strain upon strain and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says weakness upon weakness.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r1.claim: Weaning in two years means the child's rearing and nursing after birth; this matches 2:233.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r1.anchor: تربيته وإرضاعه بعد وضعه في عامين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and other imams infer a minimum pregnancy of six months by comparing thirty months for pregnancy and weaning in 46:15 with a full two-year nursing term.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r2.anchor: أن أقل مدة الحمل ستة أشهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r3.claim: Mention of the mother's toil, including nights awake, recalls her prior care and calls the child to show her kindness, as in 17:24; God will richly reward gratitude to Him and the parents.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r4.claim: Muʿādh, sent by the Prophet, tells his hearers to worship God, avoid shirk, obey the Messenger for their good, and recognize that their final destination is everlasting Paradise or Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336#2/r4.anchor: أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا، وأن تطيعوني لا آلوكم خيرا

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r3.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads “his weaning” without the alif; the other readers use the form with alif.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r3.anchor: وقراءة القراء: (فصاله) بالألف، وعن يعقوب: (فصله) بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r5.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning, named for cutting the child off from the maternal breast.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r5.anchor: والفصال: الفطام، وأصله: القطع، فصلت بين الشيئين

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r8.claim: The verse about dutifulness was revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: his mother swore not to eat until he abandoned his religion, but ate after three days when he would not recant.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r8.anchor: حلفت أمه لا تأكل طعاما حتى تموت، أو يدع دينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.claim: Hamalat-hu means his mother carried him while weakened; the phrase is circumstantial and describes weakness increasing as pregnancy grew heavier.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r1.anchor: تهن { وهنا على وهن } كقولك رجع عودا على يده ، بمعنى ؛ يعود عودا على يده ، وهو في موضع الحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.claim: Abu Amr reads wahn with both words vowelled, and the source notes the two verb forms wahan-yūhinu and wahan-yahinu.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( وهنا على وهن ) . بالتحريك عن أبي عمرو . يقال : وهن يوهن . ووهن يهن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r3.claim: A reading has fasluhu in place of fisaluhu.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r4.claim: An ashkur is an explanatory gloss for waṣṣaynā: the command is to give thanks.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r12.claim: The mother's bearing and weaning are inserted between the command and its gloss to detail her hardship, especially establish the mother's claim to care, and recall her great right.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#3/r12.anchor: لما وصى بالوالدين : ذكر ما تكابده الأم وتعانيه من المشاق والمتاعب في حمله وفصاله هذه المدة المتطاولة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r4.speaker: ابن كامل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r4.claim: The command to honor parents is universal despite its singular wording.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r4.anchor: أنها عامة وإن جاءت بلفظ خاص والمراد به جميع الناس , قاله ابن كامل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r5.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r5.claim: Alternatively, the passage specifically concerns Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and names his parents as Malik and Hamna daughter of Abu Sufyan ibn Umayya.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r5.anchor: خاص في سعد بن أبي وقاص وصي بأبويه ؛ واسم أبيه مالك واسم أمه حمنة بنت أبي سفيان بن أمية , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r6.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r6.claim: They understand it as weakness upon weakness; the poet Qanab ibn Umm Sahib uses الوهن for weakness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r6.anchor: ضعفا على ضعف , قاله الحسن وعطاء . ومن قول قعنب ابن أم صاحب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r1.claim: He explains the mother's successive burdens as hardship following hardship.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r2.claim: He explains the phrase as effort upon effort.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r3.claim: Under the weakness interpretation, one view is the child's weakness added to the mother's.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r3.anchor: ضعف الولد على ضعف الوالدة , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r4.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r4.claim: Another view is the weakness of the father's seed followed by that of the mother's seed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r4.anchor: ضعف نطفة الأب على نطفة الأم , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r5.speaker: أبو كامل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r5.claim: The child's weakness develops through successive stages from seed and clot to a fetus, bones, infant, nursing child, and weaned child.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r5.anchor: ضعف الولد حالا بعد حال فضعفه نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r6.claim: A further possible sense is bodily weakness combined with weakness of resolve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r6.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : ضعف الجسم على ضعف العزم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r7.claim: Fisal means weaning from milk; jurists disagree about whether nursing after two years establishes the same prohibition.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r7.anchor: يعني بالفصال الفطام من رضاع اللبن . واختلف في حكم الرضاع بعد الحولين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r8.speaker: الشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r8.claim: He holds that nursing even a moment after two years does not create the prohibition, based on the two-year limit and a Prophetic report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r8.anchor: لا يحرم بعد الحولين ولو بطرفة عين لتقدير الله له بالحولين ولقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا رضاعة بعد الحولين ) وهذا قول الشافعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r9.speaker: مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r9.claim: He holds that nursing can establish the prohibition for a few days after the two-year period.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r9.anchor: أنه يحرم بعد الحولين بأيام , وهذا قول مالك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r10.claim: He extends the period six months beyond two years to complete thirty months, linking it to the pregnancy-and-weaning verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r10.anchor: يحرم بعد الحولين بستة أشهر استكمالا لثلاثين شهرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r11.speaker: بعض أهل المدينة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r11.claim: Some Medinans hold that the prohibition has no fixed period and applies equally to an adult and a child.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r11.anchor: أن تحريمه غير مقدر وأنه يحرم في الكبير كتحريمه في الصغير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r12.claim: Gratitude to God is for blessing, by praise and obedience; gratitude to parents is for their care, by kindness and maintaining ties.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r12.anchor: وشكر الله بالحمد والطاعة وشكر الوالدين بالبر والصلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r13.claim: He notes that God distinguishes His own right from the parents' right by commanding gratitude to both.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r13.anchor: إن الله فرق بين حقه وحق الوالدين وقال اشكر لي ولوالديك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r14.claim: The return is to God, who recompenses the good with Paradise and the wrongdoer with the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r14.anchor: إلى الله المرجع فيجازي المحسن بالجنة والمسيء بالنار

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r15.claim: He transmits a Prophetic saying that God's pleasure follows a parent's pleasure and God's anger follows a parent's anger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p334/r15.anchor: روى عطاء عن عبد الله بن عمر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( رضا الرب من رضا الوالد

MUJAHID:v2p504#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p504#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p504#2/r1.claim: He glosses the mother's successive weakness as the hardship associated with carrying the child.
MUJAHID:v2p504#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وهنا على وهن ﴾ يعني المشقة وهن الولد

MUQATIL:31:14-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r1.claim: The parents in this passage are Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas’s father Malik and mother Hamna bint Sufyan; she bore him weakness upon weakness and weaned him over two years; thanks to God means gratitude for guidance to Islam.
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r1.anchor: سعد بن أبي وقاص بوالديه، يعنى أباه اسمه مالك، وأمه حمنة بنت سفيان بن أمية بن عبد شمس

MUQATIL:31:14-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r2.claim: Saʿd must not obey parents who urge shirk, yet should treat them kindly; he should follow the Prophet’s religion and remember that all return to God for judgment.
MUQATIL:31:14-15/r2.anchor: فلا تطعهما } في الشرك { وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا } يعنى بإحسان،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r1.claim: The mother bears increasing weakness upon weakness as pregnancy grows heavier and her weakness compounds.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r1.anchor: أى حملته تهن وهنا على وهن أى تضعف ضعفا فوق ضعف أى يتزايد ضعفها ويتضاعف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r2.claim: Weaning is complete at the end of two years.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ وفصاله في عامين ﴾ أى فطامة عن الرضاع لتمام عامين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r3.claim: The command to thank God and parents explains the prior charge; the mother's long burden is an inserted reminder of her special right.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ أن اشكر لي ولوالديك ﴾ هو تفسير لو صينا أى وصيناه بشكرنا وبشكر والديه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r4.speaker: ابن عيينة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says observing the five prayers thanks God, while praying for one's parents after each prayer thanks them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله ومن دعا للوالدين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r5.claim: The return is to God, who will hold each person accountable.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ إلي المصير ﴾ أى مصيرك إلى وحسابك على

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.claim: The two verses interrupt Luqmān's advice. One view makes them part of his advice to obey parents outside of shirk; another makes God address Luqmān with a command to thank Him; a third treats them as God's separate instruction to humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.anchor: هاتان الآيتان اعتراض بين أثناء وصية لقمان

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the correct view, held by a group of exegetes, is that these verses were revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, as previously discussed in al-ʿAnkabūt.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r2.anchor: والصحيح أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في شأن سعد بن أبي وقاص

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r3.claim: Children must not obey parents in committing a major sin or abandoning an individual duty; obedience is required in permissible matters, and yielding on recommended acts is good.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r3.anchor: طاعة الأبوين لا تراعى في ركوب كبيرة ولا في ترك فريضة على الأعيان

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan differs on one example: if a mother prevents her child from attending the night prayer out of concern, he says the child should not obey.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r4.anchor: إن منعته أمه من شهود العشاء شفقة فلا يطعها

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r5.claim: A man asked whom he should honor most; the Prophet named the mother three times, then the father, matching the verse's three maternal burdens and one paternal share.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r6.claim: The mother receives three measures of filial honor because pregnancy and nursing are singled out in addition to parenthood, while the father receives one.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r6.anchor: حصل لها بذلك ثلاث مراتب، وللأب واحدة وأشبه ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r7.claim: Wahnan ʿalā wahn means the mother carried the child with weakness increasing day after day.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r7.anchor: حملته في بطنها وهي تزداد كل يوم ضعفا على ضعف

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r8.claim: Another explanation is that women are weak by nature and pregnancy further weakens them.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r8.anchor: وقيل: المرأة ضعيفة الخلقة ثم يضعفها الحمل

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r9.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r9.claim: ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī reads both instances of wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the same reading is reported from Abū ʿAmr, and the meaning is unchanged.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15/r9.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي: «وهنا على وهن» بفتح الهاء فيهما ورويت عن أبي عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r1.speaker: قعنب بن أم صاحب
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r1.claim: Qanab ibn Umm Ṣāḥib's verse uses al-ayn and al-wahn as evidence for the word's usage.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r2.claim: The word wahn has multiple Arabic conjugations; wahnan is accusative as a verbal noun according to al-Qushayrī, or as a second object with the preposition omitted according to al-Naḥḥās.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r3.claim: Most read fiṣāluhu; al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read faṣluhu. Both are dialect forms for weaning, named by its endpoint at two years.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «وفصاله» وقرأ الحسن ويعقوب: «وفصله» وهما لغتان

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r4.claim: Jurists agree that nursing lasts two years for maintenance rulings; opinions differ on milk kinship, including one year only, two years plus an adjacent month if nursing continues, and whether milk after early weaning still prohibits.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r4.anchor: الناس مجمعون على العامين في مدة الرضاع في باب الأحكام والنفقات

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses an aškur as accusative, meaning God commanded gratitude; al-Naḥḥās prefers an explanatory particle, meaning We told the person to thank God and parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r5.anchor: النحاس: وأجود منه أن تكون «أن» مفسرة، والمعنى: قلنا له أن اشكر لي ولوالديك

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r6.claim: Some say thanks to God are for faith and thanks to parents for upbringing.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r6.anchor: قيل: الشكر لله على نعمة الإيمان، وللوالدين على نعمة التربية

QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r7.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna says the five daily prayers express gratitude to God, while praying for one's parents after them expresses gratitude to the parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:14-15#2/r7.anchor: من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r2.claim: The construction وصينا الإنسان was discussed earlier at 29:8.
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r2.anchor:
وتقدم الكلام أيضا على
وصينا الإنسان
في العنكبوت [الآية

SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r1.claim: وهنا may be a circumstantial phrase qualifying the mother, meaning weakness upon weakness, or the object of حملته, meaning successive embryonic stages; both occur in tafsir.
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r1.anchor: يجوز أن ينتصب على الحال من " أمه " أي: ضعفا على ضعف، أو من مفعول " حملته " أي: علقة ثم نطفة

SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r2.claim: He allows وهنا to be understood after an omitted preposition, meaning in weakness; على وهن then describes وهنا.
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r2.anchor: وقيل: منصوب على إسقاط الخافض أي: في وهن. قاله أبو البقاء. و " على وهن " صفة ل " وهنا

SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r3.speaker: الثقفي وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r3.claim: They read وهنا على وهن with fatḥa on both ه letters, either a dialect variant or the verbal noun of وَهَنَ.
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r3.anchor: وقرأ الثقفي وأبو عمرو في رواية { وهنا على وهن } بفتح الهاء فيهما. فاحتمل أن يكونا لغتين

SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r4.speaker: الجحدري وقتادة وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r4.claim: They read وفصله without alif, meaning his weaning.
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وقتادة وأبو رجاء/ " وفصله " دون ألف أي: وفطامه

SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r5.claim: أن اشكر is either explanatory or a verbal-noun clause governed in the accusative by وصينا; al-Zajjaj holds the latter.
SAMIN-DURR:31:14/r5.anchor: أن اشكر " في " أن " وجهان، أحدهما: أنها مفسرة. والثاني: أنها مصدرية في محل نصب ب " وصينا

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.claim: Luqmān’s warning against associating partners and the divine charge to honor parents jointly guard against two gravest sins.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.anchor: combined with the “charge”given to human beings about parents constitute protection against the two

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.claim: The Prophet identifies associating partners with God and disrespecting parents among the greatest major sins.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.anchor: the Prophet asked his Companions, “Shall I tell you what are the greatest of major sins? . . . To attribute partners to God

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r3.claim: Goodness, gratitude, and virtue toward parents are enjoined elsewhere, often alongside worshipping God alone.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r3.anchor: Goodness, gratitude, and virtue toward parents are enjoined in several verses

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r4.claim: The command to be virtuous toward parents is the first injunction of the covenant in 2:83.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r4.anchor: In 2:83, Be virtuous toward parents is listed as the first injunction of the covenant

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r5.speaker: IK, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r5.claim: “Weakness upon weakness” refers to the hardships of childbearing.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r5.anchor: Weakness upon weakness refers to the hardships of childbearing (IK, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r6.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir’s abbreviated citation also allows “weakness upon weakness” to mean exhaustion upon exhaustion.

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r7.claim: The two-year weaning period indicates that full two-year breastfeeding is best when possible.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r7.anchor: it is best for a child to be breast-fed for a full two years when possible

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r8.claim: Giving thanks to God is through praise and obedience; gratitude to parents is shown through righteousness and maintaining kinship ties.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r8.anchor: Giving thanks unto God is said to be accomplished through praise and obedience

TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r1.claim: God commanded kindness to parents; a mother bears weakness upon weakness, meaning growing weakness and hardship. Zuhayr's verse uses wahn for frailty.
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r1.anchor: يقول: ضعفا على ضعف، وشدة على شدة

TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as hardship following hardship and development following development.
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن} [لقمان: 14] يقول: شدة بعد شدة، وخلقا بعد خلق

TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses it as weakness upon weakness.
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله: " {وهنا على وهن} [لقمان: 14] يقول: ضعفا على ضعف

TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r4.claim: Qatada explains the mother's carrying as effort upon effort.
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {حملته أمه وهنا على وهن} [لقمان: 14] أي جهدا على جهد

TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r5.claim: Mujahid offers a different referent: the child's weakness layered on the mother's weakness and frailty.
TAB-FULL:v18p550#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وهنا على وهن} [لقمان: 14] قال: وهن الولد على وهن الوالدة وضعفها

TAB-FULL:v18p552/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r1.claim: God charged the person to thank Him for His favors and parents for raising and tending him through hardship until his strength matured; the person returns to God for judgment on gratitude and filial kindness.
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r1.anchor: إلى الله مصيرك أيها الإنسان، وهو سائلك عما كان من شكرك له على نعمه

TAB-FULL:v18p552/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r2.speaker: مصعب بن سعد
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r2.claim: The verse's counsel about parents was revealed concerning Saʿd: his mother refused food and drink until he abandoned Islam, then fainted and was given water by his sons.
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r2.anchor: عن سماك بن حرب، عن مصعب بن سعد، قال: " حلفت أم سعد أن لا تأكل ولا تشرب

TAB-FULL:v18p552/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r3.claim: Saʿd reports that his mother swore to starve herself unless he apostatized; relatives pried her mouth open to give her liquid, and the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r3.anchor: عن سماك بن حرب، عن مصعب بن سعد، عن أبيه، قال: قالت أم سعد لسعد

TAB-FULL:v18p552/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r4.speaker: سعد بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r4.claim: Saʿd says that after his mother refused food for three days, he swore he would not abandon his faith even if she had a hundred lives; she relented.
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r4.anchor: قال سعد بن مالك: " نزلت في: {وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا} [لقمان: 15]

TAB-FULL:v18p552/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r5.speaker: أبو هبيرة
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r5.claim: Abu Hubayra says the following instruction not to obey parents who press a person to associate partners was revealed about Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
TAB-FULL:v18p552/r5.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، قال: سمعت أبا هبيرة، يقول: قال: " نزلت هذه الآية في سعد بن أبي وقاص

ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r4.claim: Tafsir explains وهنا على وهن as weakness upon weakness: pregnancy repeatedly weakened the mother.
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r4.anchor:
جاء في التفسير (وهنا على وهن) ضعفا على ضعف، أي لزمها
لحملها إياه أن ضعفت مرة بعد مرة.

ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r5.claim: أن is accusative under وصينا; the meaning is that God enjoined the person to thank Him and his parents.
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r5.anchor:
وموضع " أن " نصب ب (وصينا).
المعنى وصينا الإنسان أن اشكره لي ولوالديك، أي وصيناه بشكرنا
وبشكر والديه.

TABATABAI:31:12-14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r9.claim: The divine instruction about parents interrupts Luqman's quoted speech to establish that gratitude to parents is obligatory like gratitude to God and is itself part of obeying God.
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r9.anchor: اعتراض واقع بين الكلام المنقول عن لقمان وليس من كلام لقمان وإنما اطرد ها هنا للدلالة على وجوب شكر الوالدين

TABATABAI:31:14-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r1.claim: Mentioning the mother's hardship in carrying and raising the child should prompt gratitude to both parents, especially the mother.
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r1.anchor: ذكر بعض ما تحملته أمه من المحنة والأذى في حمله وتربيته ليكون داعيا له إلى شكرهما وخاصة الأم

TABATABAI:31:14-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r2.claim: Wahn means weakness and is either circumstantial or an emphatic cognate object; fiṣāl is weaning, and its completion by two years means nursing lasts two full years.
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r2.anchor: والوهن الضعف وهو حال بمعنى ذات وهن أو مفعول مطلق والتقدير تهن وهنا على وهن، والفصال الفطم وترك الإرضاع

TABATABAI:31:14-15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r3.claim: Combining two years of nursing with the thirty-month pregnancy-and-weaning period in 46:15 leaves six months as the minimum gestation.
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r3.anchor: وإذا ضم إلى قوله تعالى وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا الأحقاف 15، بقي لأقل الحمل ستة أشهر

TABATABAI:31:14-15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r4.claim: “Be grateful to Me and your parents” explains the earlier command to honor them, and the return to God warns and reinforces the duty; the shift in person matches verse 31:12.
TABATABAI:31:14-15/r4.anchor: تفسير لقوله { وصينا } الخ، في أول الآية أي كانت وصيتنا هو أمرنا بشكرهما كما أمرناه بشكر الله

TABRISI:31:11-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r5.speaker: عيسى الثقفي وبعضهم عن أبي عمرو
TABRISI:31:11-14/r5.claim: A non-canonical reading has wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r5.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عيسى الثقفي ورواية بعضهم عن أبي عمرو وهنا على وهن بفتح الهاء

TABRISI:31:11-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء والجحدري وقتادة ويعقوب
TABRISI:31:11-14/r6.claim: These readers pronounce faṣluhu fī ʿāmayn with a fatḥa on the verb's ṣād.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r6.anchor: وقراءة الحسن بخلاف وأبي رجاء والجحدري وقتادة ويعقوب وفصله في عامين

TABRISI:31:11-14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r9.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:31:11-14/r9.claim: The fatḥa in wahn may reflect the influence of a guttural; faṣl is broader than separation from nursing, but fiṣāl better fits this context because it specifically concerns weaning.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r9.anchor: وأما الفصل فإنه أعم من الفصال لأنه يستعمل في الرضاع وغيره والفصال ها هنا أوجه

TABRISI:31:11-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:11-14/r12.claim: Ḥamalat-hu ummuhu is a circumstantial clause with an implied qad: the mother carries him while the person is in the state of being borne, implied by the command to honor parents.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r12.anchor: جملة في موضع النصب على الحال بإضمار قد

TABRISI:31:14-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14-15/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14-15/r1.claim: Wahnan is a verbal noun used circumstantially for an omitted tahnu; ʿalā wahn may qualify it or attach to its governing verb, while maʿrūfan qualifies an omitted noun meaning decent companionship.
TABRISI:31:14-15/r1.anchor: مصدر فعل محذوف في موضع الحال أي تهن وهنا

TABRISI:31:14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14/r8.claim: After commanding gratitude, God enjoins honoring parents as benefactors; their gratitude is paired with God's because He creates while they are the means of birth and upbringing.
TABRISI:31:14/r8.anchor: لما قدم الأمر بشكر النعمة أتبعه بالتنبيه على وجوب الشكر لكل منعم

TABRISI:31:14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r9.speaker: الضحاك والحسن
TABRISI:31:14/r9.claim: One explanation says the mother's weakness is compounded by the weakness of the father's and mother's seed.
TABRISI:31:14/r9.anchor: ضعف نطفة الوالد على ضعف نطفة الأم عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:31:14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:31:14/r10.claim: Pregnancy burdens the mother, and her weakness increases as the pregnancy advances; another view says her naturally weak constitution is further weakened by pregnancy.
TABRISI:31:14/r10.anchor: لأن الحمل يؤثر فيها فكلما ازداد الحمل ازدادت ضعفا على ضعف

TABRISI:31:14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:31:14/r11.claim: Wahn ʿalā wahn can mean hardship upon hardship and effort upon effort.
TABRISI:31:14/r11.anchor: شدة على شدة وجهدا على جهد عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:31:14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14/r12.claim: Weaning occurs at the end of two full years, the total nursing period, as in the verse about two complete years for anyone wishing to complete nursing.
TABRISI:31:14/r12.anchor: وفطامه من الرضاع في انقضاء عامين لأن العامين جملة مدة الرضاع

TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r1.claim: The mother nurses and raises her child for two years after birth, adding to her hardship; this explains the command to thank God and parents, honoring God through praise and obedience and parents through kindness and connection.
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r1.anchor: والمراد أنها بعد ما تلده ترضعه عامين وتربية فتلحقها المشقة بذلك أيضا

TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r2.claim: To God is the return is a threat: He will recompense each person according to deeds.
TABRISI:31:14-15#2/r2.anchor: وفيه تهديد أي إلي مرجعكم فأجازيكم على حسب أعمالكم

ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r1.claim: Fisāl literally describes weaning that takes place within two years.
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r1.anchor: weaning is [or "takes place"] within two years

ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r2.speaker: philologists
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r2.claim: Some philologists use fisāl for the whole period of conception, gestation, birth, and earliest infancy, when a child is wholly dependent on its mother.
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n14/r2.anchor: According to some philologists, the term fisal circumscribes the entire period of conception, gestation, birth and earliest infancy

ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n15/r1.claim: Gratitude to parents accompanies gratitude to God because parents enable one’s birth while God is the ultimate cause and source of existence.
ASAD-NOTES:31:14#n15/r1.anchor: gratitude towards parents, who were instrumental in one's coming to life

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ when he became Muslim; its story was given at the start of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في سعد بن أبي # وقاص لما أسلم، وذكرنا القصة في أول سورة العنكبوت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Kalbī, and al-Suddī gloss wahn as weakness upon weakness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والكلبي والسدي: ضعفا على ضعف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains that pregnancy weakened the mother repeatedly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r3.anchor: أبو إسحاق: أي لزمها لحملها إياه أن (¬3) تضعف مرة بعد مرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r4.claim: Wahnan is an accusative verbal noun, with the pregnancy clause implying that she weakened because she carried the child; this material is not syntactically continuous with the preceding statement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r4.anchor: وانتصب هاهنا وهنا على المصدر، ودل قوله: {حملته أمه} على أن المعنى وهنت بحملها إياه وهنا على وهن. وهذا غير متصل بالكلام الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r5.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the opening command about parents is left awaiting its complement; the pregnancy and two years of nursing detail the mother’s hardship and establish her claim, before the text resumes with the command to thank God and parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103#2/r5.anchor: فإنما عدد الله -عز وجل- ذلك ليبين وجوب حق الوالدة بما لزمها من التعب والنصب في الولادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r1.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning, separating a child from the mother so he no longer nurses; the implied construction is at the completion of two years, when the child is weaned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r1.anchor: الفصال: الفطام، وهو أن يفصل الولد عن الأم كي لا يرضع. والتقدير: وفصاله في انقضاء عامين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies the implied word completion in the phrase about weaning in two years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r2.anchor: والتقدير: وفصاله في انقضاء عامين. قاله # الأخفش (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r3.claim: The noun is the subject and the prepositional phrase its predicate; the passage highlights a mother’s two years of nursing hardship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r3.anchor: وفصاله} مبتدأ، وخبره في الظرف على تقدير: وفصاله يقع في انقضاء عامين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the command to thank God and parents as an instruction to obey them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r5.claim: Muqātil says one thanks God for guiding one to Islam and parents for the blessings they bestowed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r5.anchor: مقاتل: أن اشكر لي إذ (¬3) هديتك للإسلام، ولوالديك بما أولياك من النعم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r6.claim: The phrase explains the content of the command to the human being: God enjoined gratitude to Himself and to the parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r6.anchor: قال صاحب النظم [وقال صاحب] (¬5) المعني: ووصينا الإنسان أن اشكر لي ولوالديك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p104/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say the return is to God, who will recompense each person for his deeds.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:14-16/r1.claim: Pregnancy weakens a mother again and again, and weaning lasts two years because she nurses her child then; God commands gratitude to Him and the parents.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r1.claim: “We enjoined the human being concerning his parents” means enjoining kindness to them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r2.claim: “Weakness upon weakness” describes the mother’s repeated weakness; Ibn Mujahid, Mujahid, and Qatada offer related glosses of the child’s burden, weakness, or effort.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r2.anchor: ضعفا على ضعف، في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r3.claim: “Separation” means weaning; a Prophetic report says there is no nursing after weaning, and Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas did not count nursing after two years.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r4.claim: “To Me is the destination” means the Resurrection; reports say God’s pleasure and anger correspond to a parent’s pleasure and anger and describe Paradise or Hell’s gates for one pleasing or angering parents, even if wronged.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p674/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says good deeds have ever higher forms, culminating in giving one’s life for God, while worse sins culminate in disobeying one’s parents.

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r18.claim: The parenthetical command to honor parents is a standalone divine statement inserted while recounting Luqman's counsel, reinforcing the ban on shirk.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r18.anchor: istıtrad suretiyle mu‘teriza hâlinde başlı başına bir kelâm-ı ilâhîdir

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r19.claim: The verse, or at least its second verse, was reportedly revealed about Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r19.anchor: Sa‘d b. Ebî Vakkās radıyallâhu anh ile anası hakkında nâzil olmuştur

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r20.claim: Elmalılı reports that Saʿd refused to leave Islam when his mother threatened to starve herself; she eventually ate.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r20.anchor: yapma ana, ben bu dini hiçbir şey için terk etmem

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r21.claim: Wahn ʿalā wahn is a circumstantial description of the mother; wahn means weakness in movement, increasing weakness upon weakness.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r21.anchor: Vehn, vehn üstüne bu terkîb-i vasfî “ümm”den hâldir. “Vehn” harekette za‘ftır

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r22.claim: The apparent meaning of weaning in two years sets the maximum nursing period at two years, as held by the two Imams and al-Shafiʿi.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r22.anchor: süt kesimi de iki yılda bunun zâhirinden emzik müddetinin a‘zamîsi

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r23.speaker: İmâm-ı A‘zam
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r23.claim: Abu Hanifa instead held a thirty-month nursing period as a precaution, using 46:15, though the fatwa follows the two Imams.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r23.anchor: Lakin İmâm-ı A‘zam ihtiyat olmak üzere Sûre-i Ahkāf’ta gelecek olan

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r24.claim: Although Abu Hanifa held thirty months, the fatwa follows the position of the two Imams.

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r25.claim: The phrase "that you give thanks" explains the instruction to humanity: God enjoined gratitude to Him and to one's parents.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r25.anchor: Şükret diye bununla وَوَصَّيْنَا tefsir olunuyor. Yani şöyle: Diye tavsiye ettik ki şükret

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r26.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r26.claim: When asked whom one should treat well, the Prophet answered: one's mother three times, then one's father.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r26.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’a “ben kime iyilik edeyim?” diye sormuştu

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r27.claim: Gratitude to parents means honoring their rights through obedience, kindness, service, and prayer; the topic is also explained in Surat al-Isra.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r27.anchor: Anaya babaya şükür, haklarını gözeterek itaat ve ihsanda bulunmak ve dua etmektir. Sûre-i İsrâ’da bilhassa beyan buyurulmuştur

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r28.claim: Since the return is to God, He will question people about whether they gave thanks.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r28.anchor: Dönüş ise Banadır. Yani şükredip etmediğinizi o vakit Ben sorarım

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r3.claim: The weaning phrase indicates that two years is the normal nursing period but need not be completed; parents may wean earlier.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r3.anchor: emzirmenin normal süresi iki yıl kadar olmakla birlikte bunun mutlaka tamamlanması gerekmediğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r4.speaker: Râzî; Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r4.claim: Gratitude to God and parents is jointly commanded because God creates and sustains, while parents enable birth and care for, raise, feed, and educate a child.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r4.anchor: ana babanın da insanın hem dünyaya gelmesine vesile olması hem de hayatının en zayıf dönemlerinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r5.claim: The verse specially stresses the mother's sacrifices, indirectly indicating her greater need for attention and affection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r5.anchor: annenin fedakârlığına özel bir vurgu yapıldığı görülmekte, dolaylı olarak onun daha çok ilgi ve sevgi beklediğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r6.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r6.claim: Asked who most deserves kindness, the Prophet answered 'your mother' three times before answering 'your father' on the fourth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:14/r6.anchor: “annene” diye cevap vermiş; “Sonra kime?” denilince yine “annene” demiş; üçüncü defa tekrarlanan soruya da aynı cevabı vermiş

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو، عيسى الثقفي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r1.claim: They read وهنا على وهن with fatḥa on both hāʾs; the author allows وَهَن to be a verbal noun, by analogy with وَضَر and وَحَر.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r1.anchor: الحلواني عن شباب عن أحمد بن موسى عن أبي عمرو وعيسى الثقفي

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r2.speaker: الحسن، أبو رجاء الجحدري، قتادة، يعقوب
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r2.claim: They read وفصله instead of وفصاله. Faṣl is broader than weaning, while faṣāl better fits this nursing context; the author relates both to separation and cessation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p167/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن بخلاف وأبي رجاء الجحدري وقتادة ويعقوب

QIRAAT-ER:31:14:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:14:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:14:15#1/r1.claim: The final nūn changes from kasra to ḍamma in anu, described as phonetic assimilation before the imperative.
QIRAAT-ER:31:14:15#1/r1.anchor: Vowel change on final nūn: kasra (ani) → ḍamma (anu) — phonetic assimilation

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#3/r1.claim: Qatada explains the mother’s hardship during pregnancy as hardship upon hardship.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p106#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ حملته أمه وهنا على وهن ﴾ قال جهدا على جهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r2.claim: The parent command follows Luqman’s warning against shirk as a further call to obey God, then explains why parents deserve kindness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r2.anchor: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه: لما بين لقمان لابنه أن الشرك ظلم ونهاه عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r3.claim: One view makes the parent command part of Luqman’s advice, which God reports; another makes it God’s words to Luqman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r3.anchor: فهو من كلام لقمان مما وصى به ابنه، أخبر الله عنه بذلك. وقيل: هو من كلام الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r4.claim: A third view treats the verse as an insertion reinforcing a child’s obedience to a parent in obeying God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r4.anchor: وقيل: هذه الآية اعتراض بين أثناء وصيته للقمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r5.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the correct view is that this verse and 29:8 were revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, as a group of exegetes also held.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r5.anchor: وقال القرطبي: والصحيح أن هذه الآية وآية العنكبوت نزلتا في سعد بن أبي وقاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r6.claim: A hadith gives the mother three shares of filial kindness before the father receives one, because the mother bears pregnancy, birth, nursing, and upbringing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r6.anchor: في الحديث الأمر ببر الأم ثلاث مرات، ثم ذكر الأب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “weakness upon weakness” as successive hardship and successive stages of creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r7.anchor: وهنا على وهن، قال ابن عباس: شدة بعد شدة، وخلقا بعد خلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r8.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak explains “weakness upon weakness” as weakness repeatedly increasing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r9.claim: Qatada explains it as effort upon effort: the weakness of pregnancy, labor, and postpartum recovery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: جهدا على جهد، يعني: ضعف الحمل، وضعف الطلق، وضعف النفاس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r10.claim: The first explanations parse the phrase as a circumstantial accusative; an alternative makes it the child’s condition through successive developmental stages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r10.anchor: وانتصب على هذه الأقوال على الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r11.claim: Isa al-Thaqafi and Abu Amr in one transmission read both occurrences of “wahn” with an open hāʾ; most readers use a quiescent hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r11.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي، وأبو عمرو في رواية: وهنا على وهن، بفتح الهاء فيهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r12.claim: The open-vowel form may resemble alternate pronunciations of “hair,” or may be the regular accusative verbal noun of “to weaken.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r12.anchor: فاحتمل أن يكون كالشعر والشعر، واحتمل أن يكون مصدر وهن بكسر الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r13.claim: Most readers use “his weaning”; al-Hasan, Abu Rajaʾ, Qatada, al-Jahdari, and Yaʿqub read “his separation,” meaning weaning at the end of two years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r13.anchor: وقرأوا: وفصاله. وقرأ الحسن، وأبو رجاء، وقتادة، والجحدري، ويعقوب: وفصله، ومعناه الفطام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r14.claim: Exegetes agree on two years as the nursing period for rulings and maintenance, but disagree about the period that establishes milk kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r14.anchor: وأجمعوا على اعتبار العامين في مدة الرضاع في باب الأحكام والنفقات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r15.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r15.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers reading “that you give thanks to Me” as explanatory rather than infinitival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r15.anchor: وقال النحاس: الأجود أن تكون مفسرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r16.claim: Thank God for the gift of faith and parents for the gift of upbringing; “to Me is the return” warns during the exhortation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r16.anchor: لي: أي على نعمة الإيمان. ولوالديك: على نعمة التربية إلي المصير: توعد أثناء الوصية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r1.claim: The parent command is an interjected divine statement reinforcing Luqman's prohibition of shirk; it is not something God said to Luqman.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r1.anchor: كلام مستأنف إعترض به على نهج الإستطراد في أثناء وصية لقمان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r2.claim: An alternative makes God say this to Luqman as a further command to be grateful and care for parents; al-Bahr instead attributes the advice to Luqman and says God reports it, but the author dismisses both alternatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو من كلامه تعالى قاله جل وعلا له

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r3.claim: The command means that God enjoined people to care for their parents.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r4.claim: Wahnan ala wahn may mean the mother grows increasingly weak as pregnancy progresses toward labor, or it may refer to successive weakness from pregnancy, labor, and postpartum recovery.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r4.anchor: فالمراد تضعف ضعفا متزايدا بإزدياد ثقل الحمل إلى مدة الطلق

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r5.claim: Grammatically, wahn may be a circumstantial verbal noun with an implied possessor, an intensified noun used as a circumstantial, or an absolute object of an omitted verb; in the first constructions the clause also describes the mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r5.anchor: والمصدر حال من ( أمه ) بتقدير مضاف أي ذات وهن

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r6.claim: The circumstance may instead describe the child, which accords with Mujahid's report that the child was weak atop the mother's weakness; this avoids the objection that the child's weakness should decrease rather than increase.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r6.anchor: ما أخرجه إبن جرير وإبن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد أنه قال : ( وهنا ) الولد ( على وهن )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r7.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r7.claim: Isa al-Thaqafi and one transmission from Abu Amr read both instances of wahn with a fatḥa on hāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r7.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي وأبو عمرو في رواية ( وهنا على وهن ) بفتح الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r8.claim: The vocalization may reflect the regular Kufa pattern of moving a guttural consonant's vowel, or be the verbal noun of wahina/yawhanu; al-Qamus does not confine either of the two noun forms to a single verb pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p85/r8.anchor: فإن مصدره جاء كذلك وهذا كما يقال تعب يتعب تعبا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r1.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning and ending suckling; the reading faṣl is broader, while fiṣāl is more apt for nursing despite sharing the same root, as al-Tibi notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r1.anchor: وفصاله أي فطامه وترك إرضاعه وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Raja, Qatada, al-Jahdari, and Yaqub read faṣl in place of fiṣāl.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري ويعقوب ( وفصله )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r3.claim: The apparent reading gives nursing a duration of two years, adopted by al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and al-Tahawi, and reported from Malik.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r3.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن مدة الرضاع عامان وإلى ذلك ذهب الإمام الشافعي

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r4.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that nursing which establishes the legal prohibition lasts thirty months, citing 46:15; he argues that two named periods each receive the full stated duration, by analogy with two debts due in one year or two obligations from one debtor.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r4.anchor: وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة إلى أن مدة الرضاع الذي يتعلق به التحريم ثلاثون شهرا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r5.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r5.claim: Aisha, whose statement is treated as transmitted from the Prophet, says a child is never in the womb longer than two years, even by the time needed for a spindle's coil; thus gestation is shortened and the explicit nursing term remains, though the author says this needs discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r5.anchor: لقول عائشة الذي لا يقال مثله إلا سماعا : الولد لا يبقى في بطن أمه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r6.speaker: النحاس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas takes an ishkur li walidayk as an explanatory clause interpreting God's command to care for parents.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r6.anchor: تفسير لوصينا كما أختاره النحاس فإن تفسيرية

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r7.claim: Alternatively, it is a verbal noun with an implied li-taʿlil tied to the command, or a verbal noun in apposition to parents, meaning care for them by gratitude; mentioning gratitude to God comes first because gratitude to parents depends on it, but this last analysis is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r7.anchor: وجوز أن تكون مصدرية بتقدير لام التعليل قبلها وهو متعلق بوصينا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r8.claim: The objection that the imperative forbids explanation, rationale, and apposition is invalid; under all three parses, the account from pregnancy through weaning is a parenthetical emphasis on the mother's distinctive burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r8.anchor: وعلى الأوجه الثلاثة يكون قوله تعالى : ( حملته أمهإلى عامين ) إعتراضا مؤكدا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r9.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r9.claim: In a sound report from Bahz ibn Hakim through his father and grandfather, the Prophet names the mother three times when asked whom to honor before naming the father.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r9.anchor: كما في حديث صحيح رواه الترمذي وأبو داؤد عن بهز بن حكيم عن أبيه عن جده

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r10.claim: An Arab is said to have carried his mother to pilgrimage on his back while chanting that he carries his mother, who had carried him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86/r10.anchor: وعن بعض العرب أنه حمل أمه إلى الحج على ظهره

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r1.claim: The poem argues that a mother's pregnancy, sleepless care, feeding, and self-sacrifice make her right immense and repayment small.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r1.anchor: لأمك حق لو علمت كبير كثيرك ياهذا لديه يسير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r2.claim: One view defines commanded gratitude as obedience and pleasing acts: prayer and fasting toward God, and kinship and dutifulness toward parents.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r2.anchor: فقيل هو الطاعة وفعل ما يرضي كالصلاة والصيام بالنسبة إليه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r3.claim: Sufyan says the five daily prayers express gratitude to God, while supplicating for one's parents after them expresses gratitude to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r3.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r4.claim: Alusi treats Sufyan's statement as an illustration of some forms of gratitude, not an exhaustive definition.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r4.anchor: ولعل هذا بيان لبعض أفراد الشكر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r5.claim: The return to God explains why the command must be obeyed: people return to Him, and He repays their disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p86#2/r5.anchor: إلي المصير 41 تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بالأمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses weakness upon weakness as strain after strain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شدة بعد شدة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r4.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses it as weakness upon weakness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses it as hardship upon hardship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r6.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says pregnancy brings successive weakness and hardship to a woman; pregnancy, labor, and delivery each involve weakness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المرأة إذا حملت توالى عليها الضعف والمشقة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r7.claim: Fisal means weaning; the child is weaned over two years.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r8.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r8.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says praying the five prayers thanks God, and praying for one's parents after them thanks one's parents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r8.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة في هذه الآية: من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله،

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r5.claim: The mother carries the child in layered or physical weakness; the phrase is circumstantial, with alternate vocalizations and verb forms explaining wahn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r5.anchor: أي تضعف ضعفا فوق ضعف فإنها لا تزال يتضاعف ضعفها

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r6.claim: The child is weaned at the end of two years; a reading faṣlihi supports two years as the maximum nursing period.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r6.anchor: وفطامه في انقضاء عامين وكانت ترضعه في تلك المدة، وقرىء «وفصله في عامين»

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r7.claim: An ushkurlī explains, motivates, or apposes the parental command; mentioning pregnancy and weaning emphasizes the mother's special claim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r7.anchor: تفسير ل { وصينا } أو علة له أو بدل من والديه بدل الاشتمال،

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r8.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r8.claim: The Prophet answered that one's mother deserves the greatest care, repeating mother three times before naming the father.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r8.anchor: أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك ثم قال بعد ذلك أباك

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.claim: The return to God means He will account for gratitude or ingratitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:14-15/r1.anchor: { إلى المصير } فأحاسبك على شكرك وكفرك.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r2.claim: God follows the warning against shirk with a command to honor parents, a secondary means of one’s existence and upbringing, magnifying their right and showing that gratitude to God entails gratitude to people.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r2.anchor: أتبعه سبحانه وصيته للولد بالوالد لكونه المنعم الثاني

BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r3.claim: A report in al-Firdaws attributed to Abū al-Dardāʾ says a servant who fulfilled every obligation except filial piety would not enter Paradise; honoring parents orders the practices of monotheism, prayer, and remembrance. No grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r3.anchor: كما في الفردوس عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r5.claim: The mother is especially honored for the distinctive hardships of carrying, sustaining, and raising the child, which the father does not bear in the same way.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r5.anchor: مما حصل لها من المشقة بسببه وما لها إليه من التربية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r1.speaker: author
