BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r1.claim: ‘Weakness upon weakness’ portrays the mother carrying the child amid her own inherent weakness, compounded as pregnancy advances.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r1.anchor: أي حال كونها ذات وهن تحمله في أحشائها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r2.claim: Fīṣāl means weaning after birth; the mother’s tender care is a special favor to a child who can do nothing for himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r2.anchor: أي فطامه من الرضاعة بعد وضعه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r3.claim: The two nursing years involve hardship in sleep and waking known fully only to God; calling them ‘years’ also reflects the parents’ joy in even the child’s most demanding early care.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r3.anchor: تقاسي فيهما في منامه وقيامه ما لا يعلمه حق علمه إلا الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r4.claim: The preposition fī suggests parents may wean before the full two years when the child’s condition and welfare call for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r4.anchor: مشيرا إلى أن الوالدين لهما أن يفطماه قبل تمامهما

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r5.claim: The command to give thanks explains God’s charge: He is the true giver, while parents are causes He appointed for one’s existence and upbringing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r5.anchor: أي أوجد هذه الحقيقة ولتكن من همك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r6.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p15/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī compares creation to a tree whose fruit is the human being, its kernel rather than rind, and its completion; the human combines features of the two worlds and receives verbal revelation.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r1.claim: Both الوالدان and الأبوان designate mother and father through Arabic masculine-gender predominance, as in calling the sun and moon القمران.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r1.anchor: الوالدان مثنى الوالد والوالدة، وهو تغليب للمذكر كعادة العرب في التغليب إذ يغلبون المذكر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r2.claim: He says الوالدين suits the surrounding reference to pregnancy and weaning: the verses describe the mother, and the term evokes الولادة, which is the mother's role.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r2.anchor: لو نظرنا إلى الآية لوجدناه يذكر الأم لا الأب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r3.claim: Mentioning the parents recalls that a child is helpless and weak at birth and would perish without them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r3.anchor: ذكره بالولادة وهو عاجز ضعيف، ولولا والداه لهلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r4.claim: The wording signals that kindness and companionship should favor the mother over the father because childbirth is the mother's responsibility.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى انه ينبغي الإحسان إلى الأم أكثر من الأب، ومصاحبة الأم أكثر من الأب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.claim: The Qur'an's commands and recommendations about goodness, prayer, and care speak of الوالدين, not الأبوين; he illustrates this with 17:23, 4:36, and 6:151.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p103/r5.anchor: لا تجد في القرآن الكريم البر أو الدعاء أو التوصية إلا بذكر الوالدين لا الأبوين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1014/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1014/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1014/r1.claim: Thirty months combines two years of nursing with a minimum six-month pregnancy; Samarrāʾī says some jurists derive the minimum pregnancy term from these verses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1014/r1.anchor: العامين والثلاثون واصحة باعتبار حمله وفصاله والحمل يمكن أن يكون ستة أشهر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r1.claim: Samarrāʾī says Qur'anic commands to honor parents and prayers for them use walidayn, unlike abawayn in inheritance, hinting that the mother's claim should be greater.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r1.anchor: لم يرد استعمال (الأبوين) إلا مرة في المواريث، حيث نصيب الأب أكثر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r3.claim: Because Luqmān 31:14 mentions the mother's burden but not the father, Samarrāʾī considers walidayn the most fitting term here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p104/r3.anchor: ثم هو هنا لم يأت بالأب أصلا بل قال (حملته أمه وهنا..) ولم يرد ذكر للأب أبدا

BURHAN:v3p58/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p58/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p58/r3.claim: The pregnancy and weaning clause interrupts the command to honor parents to remind the child of the mother's hardship, giving her added emphasis because she bore burdens the father did not.
BURHAN:v3p58/r3.anchor: ومنها تخصيص أحد المذكورين بزيادة التأكيد على أمر علق بهما

BURHAN:v3p58/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p58/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p58/r4.claim: A hadith accordingly gives the mother the recommendation three times and the father once.
BURHAN:v3p58/r4.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث التوصية بالأم ثلاثا وبالأب مرة

DAMGHANI:v1p148/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r3.claim: The two years of nursing correspond to al-ḥawl as a year: 2:233 calls the nursing term two complete years, and 2:240 uses ḥawl for a year.
DAMGHANI:v1p148/r3.anchor: فوجه منها : الحول بمعنى العام قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

THALABI:v7p313/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p313/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the mother's hardship as intensity after intensity.
THALABI:v7p313/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شدة بعد شدة

THALABI:v7p313/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r4.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v7p313/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses it as weakness upon weakness.

THALABI:v7p313/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p313/r5.claim: Qatadah glosses it as exertion upon exertion.

THALABI:v7p313/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r6.speaker: مجاهد وابن كيسان
THALABI:v7p313/r6.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Kaysan gloss it as hardship upon hardship.
THALABI:v7p313/r6.anchor: مجاهد وابن كيسان: مشقة على مشقة

THALABI:v7p313/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r8.speaker: يعقوب
THALABI:v7p313/r8.claim: Yaʿqub is reported to read the phrase as his separation in two years.
THALABI:v7p313/r8.anchor: وروي عن يعقوب: وفصله في عامين

THALABI:v7p313/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p313/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
THALABI:v7p313/r9.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah says the five prayers thank God, while praying for parents after prayer thanks them.
THALABI:v7p313/r9.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة في قول الله عز وجل: أن اشكر لي ولوالديك قال: من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r28.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r28.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r28.claim: Since consensus holds that gratitude to parents requires sustained obedience, not merely verbal praise, gratitude to God likewise requires obedience and using blessings in obedience rather than sin; God is thanked through glorification, parents through provision.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r28.anchor: علم أن شكر الحق لا يكفي فيه مجرد القول ما لم تكن فيه موافقه العقل ؛ وذلك بالتزام الطاعة

BURHAN:v4p302/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r12.claim: في may mean بعد, “after,” in the statement that weaning is after two years.
BURHAN:v4p302/r12.anchor: وبمعنى بعد ﴿ وفصاله في عامين ﴾ 9 أي بعد عامين

BURHAN:v2p3/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p3/r8.speaker: علي وابن عباس
BURHAN:v2p3/r8.claim: Ali and Ibn Abbas infer that the minimum pregnancy is six months by combining the thirty-month term for pregnancy and weaning with the two-year weaning term; al-Shafi‘i adopts this inference.
BURHAN:v2p3/r8.anchor: كاستنباط علي وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BURHAN:v2p3/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p3/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURHAN:v2p3/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa infers a maximum nursing period of thirty months: the full stated term can apply to each of two matters, and the added period beyond two years is assigned to nursing because pregnancy is shorter and children transition to other food.
BURHAN:v2p3/r9.anchor: واحتج بها أبو حنيفة على أن أكثر الرضاع

AKHFASH:v2p505/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p505/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p505/r2.claim: The phrase We enjoined the human concerning his parents means that We enjoined him to do good.

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r5.claim: Al-insān in the command to honor one’s parents refers to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r5.anchor: السادس عشر : الإنسان سعد بن أبي وقاص . قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r1.claim: Some exegetes identify the human addressed in the command to honor parents with Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1016/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1016/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1016/r1.claim: Al-Aḥqāf mentions both painful pregnancy and delivery, whereas Luqmān mentions the mother's successive pregnancy hardship; the author says the two ordeals reinforce the parents' claim to iḥsān.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r1.claim: A divine injunction to honor parents removes suspicion that Luqman advises his son for personal benefit; God has no such self-interest.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r1.anchor: الموصي هو الله وليست له فيه مصلحة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r2.claim: The intensive form waṣṣā is used for weighty religious and moral matters, while awṣā is used for material matters such as inheritance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r2.anchor: والله تعالى يقول (وصّى) بالتشديد إذا كان أمر الوصية شديداً ومهماً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r3.claim: He notes one Quranic exception where awṣā concerns religion: Jesus says he was enjoined to pray and give alms, while still an infant and not legally responsible.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r3.anchor: لم ترد في القرآن أوصى في أمور الدين إلا في مكان واحد اقترنت بالأمور المادية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r4.claim: The plural “We enjoined” attributes the important good injunction to God Himself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r4.anchor: قال وصّى وأسند الوصية إلى ضمير التعظيم (ووصينا) والله تعالى ينسب الأمور إلى نفسه في الأمور المهمة وأمور الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p102/r5.anchor: ولم يقل بأبويه بل اختار بوالديه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.claim: Luqman’s counsel shows Arabs that their own sages taught what the Qur’an teaches; it contrasts blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan with the wise ancestors’ reflection, and condemns punishing children for conduct Luqman taught his son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.anchor: The succeeding verses refer to the wisdom of Luqmān and the advise he gave to his obedient son.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r1.claim: After God, parents have the greatest right because they bring a person into existence and nourish them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r1.anchor: as far as gratitude and service are concerned, the children are directed to do so in the case of both the father and the mother.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r2.claim: The parental right is gratitude and service, not worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r2.anchor: as far as gratitude and service are concerned, the children are directed to do so in the case of both the father and the mother.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r3.claim: True gratitude requires fulfilling promises; verbal thanks without fulfillment are baseless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r3.anchor: Here all the three phases of pregnancy, birth and suckling are referred to

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r7.claim: The verse names the mother’s pregnancy, birth, and suckling, but no paternal labor, so the mother has a greater right than the father.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r7.anchor: It is evident from this that a mother has a greater right on her children than a father.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r8.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says the mother’s right is three times the father’s; the author says this narrative is based on this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p111/r8.anchor: the narrative of the Prophet (sws) is based which says that the right of the mother is thrice that of a father.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r4.claim: Ibn Mujahid says the sūra has five yāʾ al-iḍāfa forms and none has a reading disagreement.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p513/r4.anchor: فى هذه السورة خمس ياءات إضافة لا اختلاف فيهن

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the mother's weakness as hardship following hardship and formation following formation.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وهنا على وهن} قال: شدة بعد شدة وخلقا بعد خلق

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r3.claim: Ata al-Khurasani glosses the phrase as weakness upon weakness.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r3.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني في قوله {وهنا على وهن} قال: ضعفا على ضعف

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r4.claim: One report from Mujahid describes the phrase as hardship associated with the child.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وهنا على وهن} قال: مشقة وهو الولد

DURR-FULL:v6p522/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r5.claim: A second report from Mujahid says the child is borne in weakness, referring to the mother's weakness.
DURR-FULL:v6p522/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وهنا على وهن} قال: الولد على وهن قال: الوالدة وضعفها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.claim: Luqman’s counsel warns against associating partners, commands kindness to parents and awareness of God, prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and patience, and rejects pride while urging humility in walking and speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.anchor: من التحذير من الإشراك ، ومن الأمر ببر الوالدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r1.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r1.claim: Asked who most deserves good companionship, the Prophet answered: your mother three times, then your father.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن قال له : من أبر ؟ ( أمك ثم أمك ثم أمك )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r2.speaker: بعض العرب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r2.claim: An Arab carried his mother to the pilgrimage on his back and recited a poem saying she had nursed him and no parent can be repaid.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r2.anchor: وعن بعض العرب أنه حمل أمه إلى الحج على ظهره وهو يقول في حدائه بنفسه : أحمل أمي وهي الحماله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r3.claim: Two years is the maximum breastfeeding period; before then the matter is left to the mother’s judgment if she sees that the child is strong enough to wean.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r3.anchor: المعنى في توقيته بهذه المدة أنها الغاية التي لا تتجاوز ، والأمر فيما دون العامين موكول إلى اجتهاد الأم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r4.speaker: الشافعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī cites the full two-year breastfeeding term as proof that milk kinship does not arise after two years; Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad share the ruling.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r4.anchor: وبه استشهد الشافعي رضي الله عنه على أن مدة الرضاع سنتان ، لا تثبت حرمة الرضاع بعد انقضائهما ، وهو مذهب أبي يوسف ومحمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa sets the breastfeeding period at thirty months.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r5.anchor: وأما عند أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه . فمدة الرضاع ثلاثون شهرا .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says that if a child weaned before age two became self-sufficient on food, later nursing is not legally effective; if the child still depended on milk, it establishes milk kinship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p501/r6.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة : إن فطمته قبل العامين فاستغنى بالطعام ثم أرضعته ، لم يكن رضاعا .
